name: Stanford Doggo
def: Open source quasi direct drive quadruped built by students for a few thousand dollars that set a vertical jumping record.
body: Doggo has four two joint legs, each driven by a pair of coaxially mounted brushless motors with almost no gear reduction, so leg forces are controlled directly through motor current. A microcontroller and off the shelf motor drivers run a state machine that produces trotting, bounding, pronking and jumping from open loop leg trajectories. Weighing under five kilograms, it jumped repeatedly to about a metre, the highest vertical jumping agility measured for a robot at the time, and its full design files were published for anyone to build.
facts: Highest vertical jumping agility recorded for a legged robot when published in 2019
Complete mechanical and electrical design released as open source
specs: Eight quasi direct drive brushless motors, two per leg
Inertial measurement unit, motor position sensing
Open loop gait state machine on a microcontroller
